title: Reactive programming: streams, observables and backpressure

videos.script: At the returns desk, books come back all day. Nobody asks for them. They simply arrive. {{desk}} Code that has to react to things like that is what this lesson is for. Most of the programs you have written pull. A loop asks for the next value when it is ready for one. {{pull}} Here the source pushes. It decides when a value moves, and the code downstream has to keep up. {{push}} You will build an observable in a page of Python. A stream with values, and then an end or an error. {{observable}} Then operators. Keep the late returns, turn days into cents, add up a running total. Each value travels the whole chain before the next one starts. {{operators}} Some streams start again for every subscriber. Others are already running, and you only see what happens after you join. {{hot}} Then the hard part. The scanner reads five books a second and the catalogue handles two. A queue between them only hides the problem for a while. {{backpressure}} When the queue is full, something has to give. You can buffer, drop, keep the latest, or make the producer wait. You will run all four on the same twelve scans and count what each one loses. {{strategies}} The lesson ends with the same ideas in RxJS, in Reactor and in Go's channels.
